answer.evidence: The main body is a raised platform. Rows 11-21 form a wide deck of horizontal plank bands, with a dark outline at row 10. The deck ends in a lighter orange front-edge line at row 20, followed by darker eave shadow at rows 21-23 (column x=8 reads L=101 then 65 then 28). Below it, rows 22-46 are a vertical south face of 25 rows with X cross-bracing. The back railing (rows 1-9) and the ladder are drawn as vertical faces, but they are thin structure and not the main volume. The silhouette narrows from 32 to 30 px at row 22, which suggests a slight inset under the deck, and there is no isometric side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a 2x2 wooden platform with a railing and a ladder. Its dark edge pixels are fully tinted (0% neutral), so the outlines lean brown beside the wood, which matches the Beodeul material-tone approach and is not a black sticker line. The measured 10 visible tones per tile is on par with the hedge reference (9) but well below the roofed well (20) and cheese stall (17), the closest structural references. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat fills, and the planks and posts show some grain. By eye, though, the wood ramp has only about 3-4 steps, the planks and posts read fairly uniform, and the lower structure is sparse with little per-plank highlight or knot detail. Compared with the stall and the well, it looks thinner and flatter, with fewer shading steps than the 5-6 Beodeul uses per material. It is cleanly drawn and structurally sound, but it falls just short of the reference richness.
